<query>I keep having this thought that parts of the town and even moments in my past have just been erased from existence, like they never happened. Could entire chunks of time or space just stop being real? If so, is that why sometimes I feel like nothing holds any meaning anymore—because parts of it aren’t even there?</query>
<response>Your reflection touches on deep philosophical and psychological questions. The idea that parts of time or reality might "erase" themselves resonates with existentialist ideas about the fluidity of meaning and the human tendency to seek coherence in a seemingly indifferent universe. While there’s no scientific evidence that chunks of time or space literally vanish, such feelings might stem from cognitive processes like memory distortions, emotional processing, or even existential anxiety. 

The sense that "nothing holds meaning" could reflect a crisis of perspective—perhaps triggered by overwhelming responsibilities (like managing a sales equipment rental business) or a recalibration of your relationship with time. Consider exploring mindfulness practices to anchor yourself in the present, or journaling to trace patterns in these thoughts. If this feeling persists, consulting a therapist might help unpack whether it’s tied to stress, depression, or a broader search for purpose. Reality, as we experience it, is shaped by perception—so while the "erasure" you describe may not be literal, its emotional weight is very real.</response>
